title: pgdelta: DR round-trip latency (EXP-20, -24; EXP-94 pending)
description: v1 against the full copies at disaster-recovery round trips, as measured. EXP-20 on cubic, EXP-24 with BBR on pgdelta's own socket, the pair that showed EXP-20's verdict for scattered changes was cubic's slow mode (EXP-21, EXP-23). Backfilled from the committed CSVs by infra/observability/backfill.py; not an evidence path - cite the write-ups. Panels use range queries reduced with lastNotNull, because each session is a flat line across its own window and the windows do not overlap: an instant query would show at most one session.

options.content:
**The DR round-trip chain, as measured.** Each ratio is v1's median time divided by a baseline's at the same condition (`RATE:RTT_MS:HOST`, so `2:60:tuned` is 2 Gbit/s, 60 ms, 128 MiB TCP buffers). **Below 1 v1 is faster**; the project reads a win against EXP-09's 0.90 band.

- **EXP-20** (Oct 25, cubic): the deciding cells. Verdict **"local changes only"** at 20, 60 and 120 ms - hot 0.31-0.63, but uniform 1% 1.70-3.20. EXP-13's expectation for scattered changes failed badly.
- **EXP-21 / EXP-23** found why, and it was not buffers or round trips: **cubic's congestion window**. v1's page stream is short and bursty (610 MB), so a lost burst set cubic's threshold low and it grew back slowly. One `pg_basebackup` stream escapes this because it sends 2.1 GB continuously. Cubic fell into that slow mode in 12 of 15 runs at 20 ms; BBR in 0 of 30.
- **EXP-24** (same session, both v1s in every repeat): with BBR on pgdelta's own socket, **v1 holds at every DR round trip, scattered changes included**. Compare `EXP-24-cubic` with `EXP-24-bbr` below - that pair is the evidence that EXP-20's verdict was cubic's slow mode, not v1's design.
- **BBR stays opt-in** (EXP-26: a BBR newcomer took 81-96% of the link from cubic traffic). That is why **EXP-94** is measuring `--hash-ahead` instead: EXP-21 said pgdelta "can avoid needing [BBR] by keeping its stream full between files", and a sender-side fix needs no host setting and is fair.

These are **committed aggregates, flat across each session's window** - the time axis carries only *when the session ran*, never a curve. Cite the write-ups, not this page.

panels.title: Scattered changes (uniform 1%): v1 ÷ fastest parallel copy
panels.description: The deciding reading. Cubic is above 1 at every DR round trip; BBR brings it below 1. EXP-20 2.58 at 60 ms default; EXP-24-bbr 1.63 there and 0.63 at 60 ms tuned.

panels.title: Local changes (hot): v1 ÷ fastest parallel copy
panels.description: Where v1's lead was never in doubt: 0.31-0.63 on cubic. BBR changes it little, as EXP-24 predicted (within 10% at every condition).

panels.title: Scattered changes: v1 ÷ one pg_basebackup stream
panels.description: The qualifier EXP-13's verdict carries. On tuned hosts one stream beat cubic v1 by about 2x for scattered changes (2.06-2.30); with BBR v1 is back under 1 everywhere.

panels.title: Local changes: v1 ÷ one pg_basebackup stream
panels.description: One stream pays the full round trip on 2.1 GB, so its disadvantage grows with the delay: v1 reaches 0.07 of it at 120 ms default.

panels.title: v1's own seconds, scattered changes (uniform 1%)
panels.description: The numerator behind the ratios: what v1 actually took. Cubic 25.5 s at 60 ms default against BBR's 16.0 s, and 23.9 s against 6.6 s at 60 ms tuned.

panels.title: The baselines' seconds, scattered changes
panels.description: Why the two ratios differ so much: one pg_basebackup stream (`full`) pays the round trip on the whole 2.1 GB, the fastest parallel copy (`b_fast`) spreads it over 8 or 16 streams.
